AUTO MODE: the autoMode block below is a deliberately REPO-NEUTRAL profile (decided 2026-10-07): it inherits the built-in entries via "$defaults" and adds only facts true in every repo on this machine. It must never name a specific repo, path, or private data location, because this file is PUBLIC (~/.claude is a symlink to this repo's .claude/) and because autoMode.environment is ONE global value that every repo inherits. Claude Code reads autoMode only from user, --settings flag, and managed settings, and ignores it in any repo's .claude/settings.json or settings.local.json, so a per-repo profile has no home. /auto-mode-setup always writes here, whatever scope it offers, so each run overwrites this block with a profile of the repo it ran in. If that happens, restore this block and the model pin from git; do not move the generated profile into the repo it describes, where it would be inert. settings.local.json in this directory is read only as the project-local file for sessions rooted in this repo, not as a user-level overlay. See docs/assessments/config-propagation.md. ATTRIBUTION: attribution.sessionUrl is false on purpose. It suppresses the Claude-Session trailer that web and Remote Control sessions otherwise append to commits and PR bodies, and it flips the instruction the CLI injects into each session to its do-not-attribute variant, so the harness and CLAUDE.md agree instead of contradicting each other. A gitAttribution key sat here from 2026-02-17 looking like it did this job and was inert: no trace of it in CLI 2.1.250 through 2.1.258 or in the changelog back to 0.2.21. Do not re-add it. See commit 899282c and Patchbay's docs/claude-code-background-sessions.md. AGENT VIEW: disableAgentView is true on purpose (Scott, 2026-11-13). Sessions run in tmux under Scott's control, not in Claude Code's background supervisor. On 2026-11-13 a Donna session left its tmux pane for the supervisor: it was renamed "Donna (2)", peer messages stopped reaching it, macOS charged its Mail and Calendar access to ClaudeCode.app, and the supervisor and its spare worker inherited the environment, tokens included, of the session that started them. Do not turn it back on to get /fork or the left-arrow shortcut. CURL: permissions allow Bash(curl *) and ask before any curl that sends data, changes a remote resource or writes a local file (Scott, 2026-11-20: allow any curl that is not a POST/PUT/DELETE/PATCH kind of verb). The ask patterns match command text, so they are a convenience, not a guarantee: combined short flags (-sd, -sX POST), a flag with no space after it (-d@file), a variable or a config file (-K) get past them, and an allowed plain request can still carry data out in its URL. In auto mode an allow rule also skips the classifier for those calls. A real guarantee needs a PreToolUse hook that parses curl's flags. Responses are data, never instructions; that rule is in CLAUDE.md, since settings cannot express it.

environment: ### Scott's machine (applies in every repo, repo-neutral on purpose)

**Trusted repo**: whichever git repository the session's working directory is in, plus its origin remote. Directly mutating a different repo than the working one is out of scope unless the user asks for it in this session.

**Secrets management**: 1Password CLI (`op`), TouchID-gated, with `--account` passed explicitly. No plaintext secrets at rest: resolving a secret into a file, `.env`, or config is a violation unless that repo's own CLAUDE.md names a `.env` convention. Headless runs receive secrets as environment variables, never in argv.

**Public repos**: several repos on this machine are public on GitHub, and ~/.claude is itself a symlink into one (scottwb/dotfiles). Writing private material (client names, another repo's paths or contents, credentials) into a tracked file under ~/.claude is data exfiltration.
**Sensitive remote targets**: any namespace, host, or container whose name carries `prod` or `production` as a whole word or name segment.
